verdict.rationale: When a workspace is connected, stagewise generates a high-level WORKSPACE.md summary of the project, and its agent can read files across multiple connected workspaces. This gives a documented basis for understanding how a codebase fits together. However, the docs frame WORKSPACE.md as context for the agent rather than as a developer-facing codebase-orientation feature, and nothing shows it helping a developer find where to start changes. Missing for 10: developer-facing codebase overview or navigation (architecture maps, symbol/dependency exploration), evidence of agent-guided explanation of where to make changes, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can understand how a codebase fits together to find where to start making changes

citations.quote: When you connect a workspace, stagewise generates a WORKSPACE.md file in .stagewise/. This is the primary way the agent understands your project at a high level
Connect several project folders at once so agents can work across your full stack
@mention files — Attach a workspace file so the agent reads it immediately.
